messages:
alex: 🚨 ACME support here — they've been seeing a sharp p99 latency regression on the embeddings and chat endpoints in us-west-2 since the overnight rollout (~11:20 UTC). Requests are hitting 2–5s and some client timeouts. They say it started right after the CUDA15 driver push.

jordan: thanks for flagging. any error codes or traces from the API gateway?

alex: gateway mostly 200s but backend shows timeouts and increased queueing. customer provided this sample: 
```
2026-03-17T11:21:55Z embed req_id=abcd1234 p95=180ms p99=2.9s backend_wait=2100ms nvme_io_wait=150ms
trace: kvcache miss -> model shard stall -> gpu queue depth climb
```

maya: noted. I just checked infra metrics — a subset of nodes in us-west-2 have host_io wait spikes starting 11:18. nvme queue depth jumped and kswapd churn looks higher on those hosts.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] CUDA15-driver-rollout completed in us-west-2 at 11:15 UTC. 12/18 nodes updated.

sre-lead: ok this smells like driver/kernel interaction causing NVMe tail latency which then backpressures KV cache and increases model latency. can we triage one affected node?

jordan: I'm going to repro locally against a copy of the customer's prompt set and target the same model. can someone pin an affected node id?

maya: node ids: usw2-n1001, usw2-n1003, usw2-n1008. n1003 shows the worst nvme_io_wait and repeated `blk_update_request` latencies.

support-eda: the customer is hitting billing concerns too — they're worried about retries and token charges during the spike. told them we're investigating and will DM a follow-up.

jordan: ssh'd into usw2-n1003 and ran: 
```bash
iostat -x 1 3
Device      r/s   w/s   rkB/s  wkB/s  rrqm/s wrqm/s  avgrq-sz  avgqu-sz  await  r_await w_await  svctime  %util
nvme0n1   50.00 0.00  1024.0 0.00   0.00   0.00     20.48     8.34    5.3   1.2     5.3     1.1     89.1
```

jordan: avgqu-sz=8.34 is high, svctime spikes present. interestingly CPU for the qemu/process isn't saturated.

sre-lead: collect `dmesg` and `nvme error-log` and also `nvidia-smi topo --list` for that node. if it's driver-induced, there might be firmware interactions.

maya: dmesg shows repeated firmware timeouts around 11:19 and kernel logged some `X255: nvme completion delayed` messages. grabbing nvme error-log now.

ops-bot: [metric-alert] us-west-2 nvme_io_wait > 120ms on 3 hosts (alert 3 of 3).

jordan: quick checklist for mitigation options: 
- move affected customer traffic to fallback pool (lower capacity but no CUDA15 yet)
- rollback driver on the worst hosts to previous version
- enable aggressive KV cache warming to reduce NVMe pressure for short term

sre-lead: agree. start failover policy for ACME to fallback pool and throttle retries. Maya, can you open a rollback play for n1003/n1008?

maya: starting rollback on n1003 now (ansible playbook: `playbooks/driver_rollback.yml --hosts usw2-n1003`). status: applying.

support-eda: told ACME we'll route them to fallback and pause billing counters for retries during investigation. they asked for ETA ~30–60 mins.

jordan: repro run against fallback pool shows p99 back to ~200–300ms. good. fallback routing seems to mitigate client-visible impact.

maya: rollback applied to n1003, kernel logs stop spamming nvme timeouts, avgqu-sz dropped to ~0.4 in next iostat.

sre-lead: good. plan: 1) continue rollback across impacted nodes, 2) open driver/firmware bug with vendor including dmesg, nvme logs, and iostat samples, 3) run a controlled canary of CUDA15 with storage IO throttling knob off to see if interaction recurs.

jordan: I'll capture a minimal repro script and dataset and attach to the bug. includes `strace` of model server showing stalls at `write()` to nvme.

maya: rolling back n1008 next. coordinating with on-call to avoid broad impact.

ops-bot: [incident-note] mitigation: ACME routed to fallback pool; nodes n1003/n1008 under rollback; monitoring set for nvme_io_wait and model p99.

sre-lead: follow-ups: 
- postmortem with timeline and cost impact to customer (support to own billing crediting)
- add e2e test that hits KV cache + NVMe under driver variants before future rollouts
- tune rollout to 25% canary with storage IO soak for 2 hours

support-eda: will draft customer communication and billing mitigation note.

aj: any objections to marking incident as mitigated once all affected nodes rolled back and customer confirmed?

sre-lead: no objections. keep thread updated.

alex: thanks team — sending update to ACME now. :white_check_mark:
